place.zh: 石坳村 · 屋后柴垛 · 夜

setup.zh: 银月钻进木牌的那天夜里，你把洗髓丹扔进娘洗衣裳的大木盆，一盆清水变成了墨绿。今夜就泡。疼，别喊。
setup.en: The night Yinyue went into the token, you drop the Marrow-Washing Pill into your mother's big washtub, and the clear water turns dark green. Soak tonight. It hurts; don't cry out.

recap.zh: 你泡了洗髓丹，一声没吭；一蹦，脑袋撞上了一丈高的顶梁。第二天，娘把那只木盆刷了三遍，什么也没问。
recap.en: You soaked in the Marrow-Washing Pill without a sound; one jump, and your head hit a beam ten feet up. Next morning your mother scrubbed the tub three times and asked nothing.

zh: 一只大木盆，一盆墨绿的水。
一蹦，撞上了一丈高的顶梁。
en: A big washtub of dark green water.
One jump — and a beam ten feet up.

story.zh:
银月化光钻进木牌的那天夜里，小满泡了她留下的洗髓丹。盛水的是他娘洗衣裳的大木盆，他怕吵醒了爹娘，从井里一桶一桶地拎到柴垛后头，拎了七桶。那颗黑乎乎的药丸扔进去，只听得「滋」的一声，化开了，一盆清水登时变成了墨绿色，咕嘟咕嘟冒着泡，那股怪味冲上来，熏得他眼泪直流。

他脱了衣裳，把那块木牌挂在柴垛的一根枝杈上，冲它道：「你看着。我不喊。」说完便一咬牙，泡了进去。
story.en:
The night Yinyue turned to light and went into the token, Xiaoman soaked in the Marrow-Washing Pill she had left. The tub was the big wooden one his mother washed clothes in; afraid of waking his parents, he carried the water from the well bucket by bucket round behind the woodpile — seven buckets. He dropped the black pill in, there was a *hiss*, it dissolved, and the clear water turned dark green at once and bubbled; the stench rose up and stung his eyes to tears.

He stripped, hung the token on a fork of the woodpile, and said to it: "You watch. I won't cry out." Then set his teeth and got in.

label.en: Get in, and not a sound

exits.means: soaks in the marrow-washing bath, endures it silently

story.zh:
不是刀割的疼，也不是摔断骨头的疼——骨头他几天前刚摔过，那种疼他认得。这是从骨头缝里往外钻的疼，从脚趾头一寸一寸钻到头发梢。他咬住了自己的胳膊，咬出了血，一声没吭。他身上不住地往外渗东西，黑的，黏的，一盆水从墨绿变成了漆黑。他疼得眼前一阵一阵地发白，白里头，有时候是他娘蹲在地上捡碗的样子，有时候是他爹吊在崖上伸下来的那只手，有时候是崖根底下，一只小手在他手里松开。

疼停下来的时候，月亮已经从柴垛这头挪到了那头。他扶着盆沿爬出来，拿井水冲了三遍，低头看自己，只见皮肤底下淡淡的有一层光，像月亮底下的一块玉。那只肿了几天的手腕，一点也不肿了。他试着往上蹦了一下，「咚」的一声，脑袋已撞上了柴棚的顶梁。「你爷爷的——」那根梁，离地少说也有一丈。他捂着脑袋蹲在地上，眼泪都疼出来了，一边疼，一边把脸埋在膝盖里笑，又怕把爹娘笑醒了。笑够了，他从枝杈上取下那块木牌，攥在手心里，道：「银月。我没喊。」木牌没有回答。

第二天一早，那只大木盆不见了。他赤着脚跑到井台边，只见他娘蹲在那里，拿一把稻草蘸着草木灰，一下一下地刷那只盆。盆里的黑水已经倒了，倒在井台底下的阴沟里，阴沟里的草一夜之间全黄了。她刷完了第三遍，把木盆翻过来扣在井台上晾着，这才抬起头来看他，先看他的脸，又看他那只左手。那只手腕上，还缠着她打的那个方方正正的结。小满把手往身后藏了藏，又觉得藏得太着急了，便又拿出来，在她面前晃了晃，龇牙咧嘴地道：「娘，还疼。」他娘看着那只手腕，看了一会儿，道：「那就再缠两天。」

她起身进屋去了，走到门口，停了一停，没回头，道：「那盆，往后晚上要用，自己拿。用完了，自己刷。」

这是他娘这辈子，头一回替他藏了一样东西。
story.en:
It wasn't the pain of a knife, nor of a broken bone — he'd taken a fall a few days ago, and knew that one. This pain drilled out from the cracks between the bones, inch by inch from his toes to the ends of his hair. He bit his own arm till it bled and didn't make a sound. Things kept seeping out of him, black and sticky, and the tub went from dark green to pitch black. The pain whitened his sight in waves, and in the white, sometimes, was his mother crouched on the floor gathering the bowl, sometimes his father's hand reaching down from the cliff, sometimes, at the foot of a cliff, a small hand letting go of his.

When the pain stopped, the moon had moved from one end of the woodpile to the other. He clambered out over the rim, rinsed himself three times with well water, and looked down at himself: under his skin was a faint glow, like jade under the moon. The wrist that had been swollen for days wasn't swollen at all. He tried a little jump — *thunk* — his head had hit the ridge beam of the woodshed. "Your grandpa's —" That beam was ten feet off the ground if it was an inch. He crouched clutching his head, tears of pain in his eyes, hurting and laughing at once with his face buried in his knees, afraid of laughing his parents awake. When he'd laughed enough he took the token down from the branch, held it in his palm and said, "Yinyue. I didn't cry out." The token didn't answer.

Next morning the big tub was gone. He ran barefoot to the well and found his mother crouched there, scrubbing it with a wisp of straw dipped in ash, stroke after stroke. The black water had been tipped into the ditch below the well, and the grass in the ditch had turned yellow overnight. She finished her third scrubbing, turned the tub upside down on the well-edge to dry, and only then looked up at him — first at his face, then at his left hand. Round that wrist was still the square, neat knot she had tied. Xiaoman tucked the hand behind him, then felt he'd been too quick about it, brought it out again and waved it in front of her, wincing: "Ma, still hurts." His mother looked at the wrist a while. "Then keep it bound two more days."

She got up and went in; at the door she stopped, and without turning round said: "That tub — if you want it at night, fetch it yourself. When you've done, scrub it yourself."

It was the first time in her life his mother had hidden something for him.

refuse.zh: 三炷香还没烧完。疼，别喊。
refuse.en: The three sticks of incense haven't burned down. It hurts — don't cry out.

label.en: It hurts too much — climb out

exits.means: gives up the bath, climbs out

story.zh:
小满一只手扒上了盆沿。

挂在枝杈上的木牌凉凉的，那一条银色的尾巴，一明，一暗。她说：疼，别喊。她没说可以出来。

他的手，一点一点地松开了。他沉回那一盆墨绿的菜汤里。
story.en:
Xiaoman got one hand over the rim of the tub.

The token hanging on the fork was cool; its one silver tail went bright, dim. She'd said: it hurts, don't cry out. She hadn't said he could get out.

His hand let go, bit by bit. He sank back into the tub of dark-green soup.
